groupRulesOneTitle: Feeling safe in a trusting environment
groupRulesAttencion: Please carefully read the 14 group rules
groupRulesOneParagraphOne: It is very important for all group meetings that you uphold the group rules. These group rules help ensure that a safe and trusting environment is created for each and every member.
groupRulesOneParagraphTwo: Your group should provide a place that you should feel comfortable and can open up in. It gives you the opportunity to discuss things that are on your mind in a trusting environment, outside of the chaos of everyday life.
groupRulesTwoParagraphOne: Everything that is discussed within the group, stays within the group. Every member strives to create a friendly atmosphere, in which all can feel comfortable in.
groupRulesTwoParagraphTwo: We treat each other with respect and are kind to one another.
groupRulesTwoParagraphThree: We let each other talk and do not criticise one another.
groupRulesThreeParagraphOne: Together, we ensure that all members get the same opportunity to share.
groupRulesThreeParagraphTwo: We actively listen – sometimes just listening to one another is worth more than constant comments and advice.
groupRulesThreeParagraphThree: Every topic, every problem will be taken seriously.
groupRulesFourParagraphOnePartTwo: We use these to express/phrase our own emotions, opinions, assumptions or perceptions. Therefore, we avoid phrases such as
groupRulesFourParagraphOnePartThree: Instead, a sentence could start with
groupRulesFourParagraphOneItalicThree: “I have had positive experiences with.../I found it helpful when...”.
groupRulesFourParagraphTwo: It is helpful, to regularly be aware of one self – your body, your thoughts, your feelings.
groupRulesFiveParagraphOne: We also talk to each other, not about each other. Absent group members will not be subject of converstation.
groupRulesFiveParagraphTwo: Individual responsibility: every member of a group is responsible for what they do and/or say. Appreciation and respect for yourself and others is important, that means I respect my own boundaries and possibilites as well as those of my group members.
groupRulesSixParagraphOne: The camera should remain on during sessions so that you can all see each other and no member is forgotten.
groupRulesSixParagraphTwo: Take some time and relax before a session.
groupRulesSixParagraphThree: Be patient with others, but especially with yourself - be kind to yourself.
groupRulesSixParagraphFour: Last but not least: Have fun!

mentalHealthIntroTextOne: A good mental health is vital to successfully improve your lifestyle.
mentalHealthIntroTextTwo: To tailor the program to suit your needs you will be asked questions in the next section regarding your current well-being, physiological symptoms, possible anxiety symptoms and mood. This should take around 10 minutes.
mentalHealthIntroTextThree: You can take a break inbetween. If you do take more than an hour to complete all questions you will be asked to start this section again. You will receive your results immediately after the questions. Please note that these test results are not a diagnosis. A diagnosis can only be made by a doctor or psychologist.
who5ResultTestMinimal: Regarding your general well-being, you have indicated that in the last two weeks your well-being has been severely limited, and you have felt unwell most of the time. If you feel unwell for a longer period, we recommend that you consult a psychologist or your doctor to check these symptoms. You can find psychologists here:
who5ResultTestHigh: In terms of your general well-being, you indicated that you have generally felt balanced, joyful, and relaxed over the past two weeks. This result indicates a good state of well-being.
phq15ResultMinimal: You have stated that you have had no or few physical symptoms in the last four weeks. That’s great.
phq15ResultMild: You have stated that you have been bothered by a few physical symptoms in the last four weeks. This is not a cause for concern. This could be a temporary reaction of your body to stress. Try to reduce a little stress in your life.
phq15ResultMedium: You have stated that a number of physical symptoms have bothered you over the past four weeks. A consultation with your doctor is recommended to check whether these symptoms are temporary. The symptoms can be a reaction of your body to stress or emotional issues.
phq15ResultHigh: You have stated that many physical symptoms have bothered you in the last four weeks. Please consult your doctor to check these symptoms. These symptoms may have a medical cause or indicate a somatization disorder.
gad7ResultMinimal: You have stated that you were at ease most of the time in the last two weeks. Your everyday life is not effected by anxiety. Great, keep it up.
gad7ResultMild: You have stated that in the last two weeks you have had problems to relax from time to time. You may also have felt nervous, anxious or on edge. Don’t be concerned about it. These may be temporary symptoms. Give yourself a break to relax more often. But if the symptoms worsen, we recommend a consultation with a psychologist.
gad7ResultMedium: You have stated that you have felt nervous or anxious more than half the days in the last two weeks. You may also have not been able to stop or control worrying. This can be a burden for you in your daily life. If the symptoms persist or worsen, we recommend a consultation with a psychologist
gad7ResultHigh: You have stated that you have felt nervous or anxious nearly every day in the last two weeks. You may also have not been able to stop or control worrying. These symptoms could indicate an anxiety disorder. In order to have a closer look at the symptoms and to treat them, if necessary, we recommend consulting a psychologist. You can find addresses here:
ifYouHaveSuicidalThoughts: If you are in an acute crisis or having suicidal thoughts, please contact one of the 24-hour toll-free emergency numbers immediately:
phq8ResultMinimal: You have stated that your mood was not affected most days in the last two weeks. Great, keep it up and look out for all the positive things you will come across on your journey.
phq8ResultMild:
You have stated that in the last two weeks you have felt down from time to time. You may also have had feelings of hopelessness or lack of energy. Throughout the LeanOnMe program, you will learn about the connection between thoughts and feelings and what you can do to improve your mental health.
If the symptoms worsen, we recommend a consultation with a psychologist.
phq8ResultMedium: You have stated that you have been depressed more than half the days in the last two weeks. You may also have had feelings of hopelessness or have felt down. Throughout the LeanOnMe program, you will learn about the connection between thoughts and feelings and what you can do to improve your mental health. If the symptoms persist or worsen, we recommend a consultation with a psychologist.
phq8ResultHigh: You have stated that your mood has often been significantly effected in the last two weeks. You have indicated that you have felt depressed and have often suffered from listlessness or dejection in the last few weeks. The symptoms indicate current psychological distress with emotional impairment. These may be indications of a temporary depressive episode. This program is not a substitute for mental health diagnosis or psychological treatment. In order to have a closer look at the symptoms and to treat them, if necessary, we recommend consulting a psychologist. You can find addresses here:
phq8ResultHighest:
You have stated that your mood has been significantly effected almost every day for the past two weeks. You have indicated that you have felt depressed and have often or constantly suffered from listlessness or dejection in the last few weeks. These symptoms currently indicate a  high level of psychological distress with emotional impairment and could be an indication of depression.

This program is not a substitute for mental health diagnosis or psychological treatment. In order to have a closer look at the symptoms and to treat them, if necessary, we recommend the clarification by a psychologist. You can find addresses here:
